notes.urn:cts:latinLit:tmp1062.tmp1062.opp-lat: Line 3: 'una servitute ... venerandus' is odd; perhaps for 'una veneratione' (one worship); rendered literally. 'Neque Deum aut Dominum, Christi verbum, Dei Patris asserite' read as 'do not call the Word of God the Father God or Lord of Christ' (cf. Cyril's anathemas); the printed punctuation is confused. 'Christi genitricem' rendered 'Mother of Christ'. Line 4: 'ignis gehennae' is a disease name (possibly ergotism, 'St Anthony's fire'); kept literal. 'Blandinensem' taken as the abbey of Blandin (Ghent); identification uncertain. 'paranymphum coelestem' = Gabriel, rendered literally as 'heavenly groomsman'.

In the sermon, the passage from 'De Spiritu quoque sancto' to 'non est alie[nus]' has the beginnings of words cut off in the scan (e.g. 'iristum', 'nfitemini', 'ia', ';et', 'ritus'); translated as reconstructed (cf. Cyril of Alexandria's letter to Nestorius); 'me superior, memelior' read as 'non superior, nec melior'. 'upplicium', 'acrificium', 'ternas' read as supplicium, sacrificium, aeternas. 'Censorinus Caesar' could not be identified. In the last paragraph: 'eserare' read as sperare and 'denebant' as dolebant; 'virtutem exaequamini' is unclear (rendered 'be equal in virtue'); 'putris sumus' is perhaps corrupt (for 'pulvis', 'dust'?). 'a sancto ejusdem capite, et ut ab utroque latere' is garbled; rendered 'from his holy head and from both his sides'.

Line 8: '(furte a Deo;' is read as the edition's variant 'forte a Deo' ('perhaps: from God'), rendered in parentheses as printed. 'perhibens' near 'resurrexisse' is read as 'perhibemus' ('[we] testify'). Line 10: 'qui infernus est' is read as 'qui infirmus est' ('he who is weak'), which suits the Pauline quotation. 'inter vitia ... animalia' is read as 'inter vilia' ('among lowly animals'). 'in canis' is read as 'in cunis' ('in a cradle'). 'hactenus sedere in sordibus' is rendered 'rather', reading 'potius'; the transmitted word is doubtful. 'fert esse discipulos' is taken as 'makes [them] disciples'. The opening Job quotation (Job 40:11) refers in the source to Behemoth, though this sermon applies it to Job.

In the Annunciation sermon the printed text repeats a clause ("dignior quae per aurem concipit; dignissimus autem qui nuntiat"), apparently by dittography; it is translated once. "Virginem de Virgine nasciturum" (masculine participle) seems to mean the virgin Christ born of the Virgin Mary; rendered accordingly. "in omnes" is taken as "through all" (cf. Eph. 4:6). In the prayer, "cum quo omnia Filius fecit" is rendered literally, "with whom the Son made all things".

Several evident corrections adopted: 'corna descipulorum' read as 'corda discipulorum' (hearts of the disciples); 'alterius de alterno' as 'aeternus de aeterno'; 'Mitte me' as 'Permitte me'; 'quiesbenedictus' as 'qui es benedictus'; 'largire fidero' taken as 'largire fidem' (grant faith), uncertain. The clause 'qualiter pro fide catholica... delectari, clementia tua non ignorat' is syntactically defective and is rendered by sense. The phrase rendered 'the flesh made [his] is life-giving' (vivificatricem et propriam ipsius Verbi carnem esse factam) echoes Cyril of Alexandria's eleventh anathema; the Latin is compressed. The Christological language here suggests a later composition than the attributed author.

nodes.text: SERMONS OF ST ELEUTHERIUS.
SERMON, OR CONFESSION, ON THE HOLY TRINITY.

Most beloved, confessing Christ Jesus, Lord of all, and venerating the holy Trinity in unity, be subject to him alone, fear the immortal God, to whom is honour for everlasting ages. The holy Trinity is God, since indeed the one God, the Father of the living Word, is the perfect begetter of the perfect, who neither had a beginning from anyone, nor will hold an end from anyone. For by what reasoning would the unbegotten Father of the only-begotten Son have his being from another, he who was and is the Alpha and Omega? But the only Son of God willed to be born of the one God the Father, he who is the wisdom of the Father, through whom all things were created that exist, that flourish, that have flourished, that will be born, that will perish. True Son from true Father, eternal from eternal, immortal from immortal, incorruptible from incorruptible, invisible from invisible; and one Holy Spirit, in whom the perfect life of believers abides, in whom is holiness, and the fount of holiness, and the minister of true edification: through whom God [is] in all believers and over all, and the Son, who [is] through all. But although the Father has his being from no one, and the Son obtains his origin from him, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from both, yet these are not three gods, but one true God, whose Trinity in persons is to be venerated, whose unity in substance is to be adored. The Trinity [is] perfect glory, an everlasting kingdom, a kingdom perpetual and undivided. For never was the Son lacking to the Father, or the Spirit to the Son. The Father [is] equal to the only-begotten Son; the Son [is] equal to the unbegotten Father according to the power of the Godhead, but less in his taking up of our humanity. The Holy Spirit also is not less than the Father and the Son, but coeternal, the comforter of those who mourn, the strength of the frail, sevenfold, everlasting, and the most subtle bestower of grace. The true Son, the true image of the Father's light and the true splendour of the inner brightness, willing all men to come to the knowledge of his name, came down from heaven to earth for their salvation and the washing away of sins. He was made flesh, he was made man, he suffered, and then became obedient even unto death. Of his obedience the apostle Paul bears witness, saying: Though he was the Son of God, he learned obedience from the things which he suffered; and being made perfect he became for all who obey him the cause of eternal salvation, called by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek. The same Christ also rose from the dead on the third day, then ascended into the heavens from which he had come down, and by his wonderful power led our captivity captive. Let all, therefore, who serve the catholic faith believe that he will come from there and judge the dead and the living. But those who assert that Christ is changeable or alterable the holy and catholic Church must anathematize. So, made man, that is, taking flesh from the holy Virgin Mary, although he was made [man] in the assumption of flesh and blood, yet he remained what he was, namely God, by nature and in truth. Do not say that the flesh was turned into the nature of the Godhead, nor that the inseparable essence of God the Word was changed into the substance of flesh. For he is inseparable, unchangeable, and unalterable, and according to the Scriptures he remains the same, the almighty Lord, who is blessed for ages of ages. He cannot be greater, he cannot be less; he cannot be bounded by magnitude, nor contained by time. For what is heavenly or divine is known to be without quantity and without bulk, and is held within no limits. Confess the Word of God according to subsistence; adore one Son and our Lord Jesus Christ; do not set God and man apart and separately, as though joined to each other by a unity of dignity and authority; and do not name as Christ, specifically, God the Word who is from God, nor likewise another Christ, specifically, who was born of a woman. But acknowledge, venerate and adore only one Christ, the Word of God the Father, with his own flesh. For Christ is one, Son and God, not as though some sort of conjunction of man and God were held in a unity of dignity and authority. Can equality of dignity alone unite a nature? Far from it. For Peter, shepherd of the Lord's flock, and John, the chosen virgin, evangelist and apostle, are of equal dignity with each other: for which reason they are called disciples of Christ and fit witnesses of the truth. Yet the two of them are not one. You, therefore, my dearest little sons, do not assert that the Word of God the Father is the God or Lord of Christ, lest you again more openly divide into two the one Christ and Lord, and fall into the crime of sacrilege, making him God and Lord of himself. God the Word was indeed united, as we have said, to flesh according to subsistence. He is indeed God, ruler of all, creator of the whole universe, and redeemer of men by his most precious blood. But he plainly denies the unity who divides into two Christs him who is one: he is an apostate, and truly wretched, truly to be subjected to perpetual torment. The devil and his angels rise up to seize him, the evil spirits run to receive his soul; countless torments are prepared for him, and the evils he did in his life are set before his eyes. So, lest you come into these terrible places, confess that one Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, is to be understood, to be venerated with one service together with his own flesh. Confess with a pure mind, praise with a perfect heart, glorify with a kindly mouth him who was born of God the Father, the only-begotten Son, God. Although according to his own nature he remained free of suffering, yet for us, according to the Scriptures, he suffered in the flesh; and he was in the crucified body, impassibly referring to himself the suffering of his own flesh. By the grace of God he tasted death for all men, even handing over his own body, although by nature he himself is life and the resurrection of the dead. For in order that he might trample death underfoot by his ineffable power, his wonderful strength and his inestimable majesty, and might first in his own flesh become the firstborn from the dead and the firstfruits of those who sleep, and make a way for human nature to return to incorruption, by the grace of God he tasted death for all, as has been said, and rising on the third day he despoiled the most savage jaws of hell. And therefore, although it is said that the resurrection of the dead came about through a man, you must understand the man made [to be] the Word who is from God, and that through him the dominion of death was destroyed. And as Scripture bears witness, In the last times the one Son and Lord will come in the glory of the Father, to judge the world in equity. It is necessary too that you believe the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ, his nativity, circumcision, manifestation, Gospels, passion, death, resurrection, and ascension into heaven. For this is the right faith. But since a virgin conceived, a virgin bore, God united with flesh according to subsistence, therefore confess her to be the Mother of Christ: not that the nature of the Word received the beginning of its existence from flesh. For in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God: and he is the founder of the ages, the Father of the universe. There are three who bear witness in heaven, the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit: and these three are one. Therefore confess the creator of all as one in substance, a Trinity in persons, that you may be worthy to come to the heavenly joys where the merits of the saints flourish, whose joy and exultation will not cease for ever and ever, our Lord Jesus Christ reigning with the coeternal Father, the grace of the Holy Spirit working with [them], to whom be praise and dominion through all ages of ages. Amen...
THE PASSING OF ST ELEUTHERIUS, BISHOP.

In those times, while the blessed Eleutherius presided as second bishop of the Church of Tournai, a great dispute arose among the clergy of Tournai. For certain heretics were putting forward novelties of their own heresy and trying to destroy the preaching of the truth, daring to corrupt the mystery of the divine dispensation, and denying that the heavenly groomsman had announced the Virgin's childbearing. Other heretics, bringing in confusion and wrongly compounding the flesh and the Godhead into one nature, spread abroad that by such confusion the divine nature of the Only-begotten was capable of suffering, and shamelessly asserted that he who was born of the most blessed Virgin Mary was a mere man. Others again opposed the Holy Spirit. But others, devoted to God and serving him, believed the truth and did not obey falsehood. So great was the dispute among them that the heretics even attacked the catholic sons of the Church of Tournai, and cut down many and drowned them in the river called the Scheldt. At that same time the blessed bishop of the Church of Tournai had gone to Rome, and had brought back with him the head of Mary of Egypt. He received it secretly from the Roman Church of the blessed apostle Peter, and brought it to the church of Mary, Mother of Christ. In this way, then, the man of God, returning from Rome, was received with great rejoicing by all the people. The clergy rejoiced and, dressed in dalmatics, went out to meet their blessed shepherd; but unexpectedly the joy of all was doubled. For the bishop himself was bringing the relics of blessed Mary, who endured so many and such great evils. And as he entered the Nervian Gate, a great miracle was shown by God in that very place. For as the people ran to meet him rejoicing, and likewise the ranks of clergy, the blessed bishop, wearing the pallium, climbed the hill which was called the Hill of the Hidden Treasure, but is now called the Hill of St Andrew, and showed all the people the relics of St Mary of Egypt and the shoulder of blessed Stephen the protomartyr. Suddenly a brightness coming from heaven appeared around the relics of the head of St Mary, and it was seen by all until he entered the church of the Mother of Christ. Over the shoulder of blessed Stephen a brighter radiance was seen, in the shape of a circle as if of silver. And as he entered the church, surrounded by the throng of all the people, four men and two women were in danger from a grave sickness which is called the fire of Gehenna. Then the man of God, moved by pity, placed the head before the women and the shoulder before the men, saying: Let us all pray. And as they lay prostrate and prayed, he said: St Stephen, protomartyr, help these men; St Mary, have mercy on this female sex. For we shall certainly not rise from prayer until they are made whole. At this word all were set free. And the flesh which they had lost in that sickness was restored in that very hour. A mute man standing by also spoke, saying: Behold the relics of blessed Stephen and St Mary. Then all were astounded and marvelled. In those times the relics of the saints were not placed in gold or silver. These things were done on the Nones of October. Now blessed Eleutherius had already ruled the Church of Tournai for thirty-one years, and that of Blandin for nine. Hearing that the sons of the Church were troubled, he grieved. Then by the authority of the Roman pope he decreed that all heretics should be cast out of that city, so that they might with one mind confess Christ, the Son of God the Father. So, compelled by the bishop, they chose a suitable day on which Eleutherius, bishop of Christ, should convene his synod. The day came on which the synod had been convened; the catholic sons came too, confounding the sect of the heretics, and some of the heretics were also present, contradicting them. Then the holy man of God Eleutherius rose and, motioning with his hand for silence, said: All you who confess the Lord, the Father and his Son, with the Holy Spirit, listen.
SERMON ON THE TRINITY.

Believe in one God, the Father almighty, and in his only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who was born of God the Father as the only-begotten Son, immeasurable from immeasurable, immortal from immortal, invisible from invisible, everlasting from everlasting, through whom and with whom the Father made all things that are contained in heaven, or on earth, or in the sea. I urge you therefore, most beloved: believe that our Lord Jesus Christ came down from heaven for the salvation of men and the liberation of the world, was made flesh, became man, and suffered under Pilate the governor; further, that on the third day he rose from the dead, and ascended again into heaven, from where he had come down. These decrees, my dearest sons, you must hold and observe. You must devoutly obey them if you wish to merit the heavenly joys. Obey these doctrines and decrees of the ancient Fathers, considering and seeing most clearly what it is for the Word of God to have been made flesh and made man. For you must not assert that the nature of God was changed, but rather that he joined to himself flesh animated by a rational soul, and that Christ the Son of God became man blamelessly, ineffably, substantially, and was also called the son of man. Thus Christ Jesus, who was born of the eternal Father before all ages, was also begotten in the flesh of a woman, that is, of the blessed Virgin Mary: not that his heavenly nature took its beginning from the holy Virgin, nor that for his own sake he needed to be born a second time, after that glorious birth which he had from the Father. For it is not fitting, but rather foolish, to affirm that Jesus Christ our Lord, who is coeternal with the Father before all ages, after his generation from the Father needed another, so as to begin to exist through the one which he took up in the virgin. But let the holy catholic universal Church affirm and believe that for the salvation of men and the washing away of sins he joined human nature to himself, and came forth from a virginal womb, an undefiled womb, kept most worthily by the heavenly angels. Therefore the catholic Fathers assert, and we too on the authority of our elders, that he was born in the flesh. He, kind and merciful, wishing to turn all to the path of the Godhead, joined flesh to himself from that virginal and uncontaminated womb, as was said above, and underwent a birth in the flesh, making the birth of his flesh his own. Next, believe that he was crucified and rose from the dead on the third day: not that God the Word in his own nature was struck with blows under Pilate the governor and then fixed to the gibbet of the cross, or that he endured for us the piercings of the lance and the nails and such great wounds (for God is incorporeal and beyond suffering), but because that body which became his own endured these things for us. For this reason he is said to have suffered all these things for all men, for the redemption of sins. For in that body which suffered was God, who could in no way suffer. In the same way you must understand his death. For the life-giving Word of God is by nature incorruptible and immortal. But since by the grace of God his own body, according to the saying of Paul, the teacher of the gentiles, tasted death, therefore God is said to have suffered death for us: not that he himself experienced death as far as his own nature is concerned (for it would not be fitting but absurd to assert this), but that, as we said above, his true flesh tasted death. So too, as his flesh rose again, assert the resurrection: not that he fell into corruption, but that his body rose. Therefore, most beloved, I beseech your brotherhood that you devoutly venerate the true God and his Son Jesus Christ our Lord: adore [him] with a kindly heart, praise [him] with a pure mind, confess [him] with tearful sighs, not glorifying him in word as a man, lest you introduce some appearance of division, but honour one and the same: for his body (with which he also sits beside the Father) is not foreign to the Word. Nor should you bear witness as though two sons sat beside [the Father], but one with the flesh through unity. Moreover your faith must believe that Christ our Lord was made mediator between God and men, and reconciler to peace with God the Father for us, offering himself for an odour of sweetness. For this reason he said through the prophet: Sacrifice and offering you did not want; burnt offerings for sin did not please you, but a body you have made ready for me. At the head [of the book] it is written of me that I should do your will, O God. For he offered his own body not for himself but for us, for an odour of sweetness. My brothers, which of you would doubt any longer that the true and spotless Lamb was sacrificed for the salvation of the human race, and crucified by the impious Jews? It is he who redeemed us by the wonderful strength and ineffable power of his divinity, conquered the rebellious and proud Jews, despoiled the bars of Gehenna, leading out the captives from their chains, sending forth the imprisoned from the places of darkness, who cried out and said: O good triumpher over the world, mighty vanquisher of the devil's deceit, for you, most merciful Jesus, our laments waited in these torments and pains; for you, merciful Christ, the sighs of the weeping cried out in the places of gloom. Behold, you have come, whom we have awaited from ancient times. Free us, you whom we once devoutly worshipped when we were set on earth. It is he who, after the destruction of the devil and the liberation of the saints crying out from the darkness, rose on the third day, and ascending into the heavenly kingdom sits at the right hand of God the Father. He is the Son of Mary, who as a virgin conceived by the Holy Spirit, who in unblemished virginity bore God and man, who also after the birth remained Virgin and Mother of the Saviour. He, as was said above, offered himself as a spotless victim, a victim pleasing to God the Father. But if anyone says that he offered himself to God as a sacrifice as much for himself as for us, he will not escape the final punishment, but will pay eternal penalties in destruction with the impious. Concerning the Holy Spirit also, when he said to his disciples: He will glorify me, understanding this, sons, [to mean] one Christ and Son, not as one in need of another's glory, confess that he obtained glory from the Holy Spirit: for that same Spirit is not superior to him nor better than he. And although the Spirit is in his own substance, and is understood in person by his own property, according as he is Spirit and the Son [is Son], yet he is not foreign to him. For he is called the Spirit of truth, and Christ is the truth. Therefore the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Son in the same way as from the Father. For the Holy Spirit, working miracles through the hands of the holy apostles, glorified God, Jesus Christ, after he had ascended by his glorious resurrection into heaven (from where he had come down for the liberation of our souls): therefore by us and by not a few catholic men Christ is believed to be God existing by nature, showing through his Spirit mighty works and glorious miracles to the nations scattered through the whole world. Hence our Lord Jesus Christ said: He will receive of mine, and will announce [it] to you. But in no way is the same Holy Spirit said to be powerful or wise by participation in another, for he is perfect through all things and in all things, and lacks no good at all. For the Holy Spirit is believed to be [the Spirit] of the Father's power and of the heavenly wisdom, that is, of the Son, and for that reason, subsisting in very reality and power, he is proved to be power and wisdom. Most beloved brothers, this is the right faith, to be held by all catholic men; and unless each one believes it firmly and rightly, he cannot be freed from fellowship with the devil. Confess one in substance, threefold in persons, that you may be worthy to come to the heavenly kingdom and rejoice for ever in eternal goods; where the angels rejoice, the apostles are glad, the glorious throng of martyrs exults, the band of confessors and virgins applauds, whom the Redeemer of the world crowns with an everlasting laurel, who lives and reigns, God almighty, invisible, eternal, incorruptible, to whom is honour, praise, glory and dominion, unfailing power, unfading majesty, perpetual glory and ineffable might, with the Father and the Holy Spirit through infinite ages of ages. Amen.

But if anyone contradicts these decrees, let him be anathema from the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Having said this, the blessed bishop Eleutherius sat down. And the catholic men who had been called to the holy synod, raising their voices with joy, glorified God, saying: We venerate and worship the Trinity in unity, we profess the unity in substance and devoutly adore [it]; on the other hand let the heretics be confounded. Then they withdrew from the sacred synod confounded. When the synod returned home, holy Eleutherius likewise went back with the catholic men to his residence, which was in a town, being now seventy-one years old. Meanwhile for five years, which the most invincible bishop lived on, the Church of Tournai was exalted by catholic men. In the meantime the party of the heretics was confounded. What were they to do? They took counsel, they inquired what should be done about him, and they said: If he prevails like this among us, our life will be despised; but if we prevail, we shall have won the victory of praise. While they were talking thus one day, behold, the blessed bishop was coming out of the church of blessed Mary of Tournai with Athanasius the deacon and Audoenus, his faithful disciple; seeing him, the heretics, hidden behind a corner (for they lay in wait for him in many ways), said: Behold the destroyer of our law; come, let us kill him. So, raising clubs, they beat him harshly, and having left him half-dead before the church, with wounds laid on him, they went away in secret. The disciples likewise abandoned their shepherd and fled. When Censorinus Caesar heard this, he would have fixed them all to the gibbet of the cross, had not the prayer of the man of God prevailed. There was an uproar of the people through the city: young men shout, matrons mourn, and virgins sprinkle themselves with ashes, old men vie to see the half-dead bishop; but he lay lifeless, and blood flowed from his holy head and from both his sides. Then a haircloth bed having been prepared by the citizens of the city, as he himself had asked, he was carried into his house; and living afterwards for five weeks, in that very sickness he gave sight to a blind man and healed a number of the sick. Then the end of the days of most blessed Eleutherius drew near; he called together his brothers and the followers of the true religion, received the body and blood of Christ openly, and foretold that in that same week he would pass out of the prison of the body. What were they to do? They saw their father hoping for heavenly things, and grieved that he was now leaving the Christians; and he, speaking gently to them, said: As I am about to enter upon the end of all flesh, and to receive the eternal joys promised me by the Lord, I urge you, dearest ones: flee hatreds, sow concord, scatter schisms, be equal in virtue, endure temporal ills for the sake of your judge, so that you may be worthy to show Christ fruit worthy of repentance. For every man is grass, and his flesh like the stubble of the field. In the morning it flourishes green; in the evening it falls dry and becomes worthless. Be patient, remain chaste, fear the Lord, persevere in all good things. For you have heard David saying: Man has become like vanity. So we are rotten [flesh]; we shall rise in the judgment; before the tribunal of Christ, as Scripture testifies, we shall all stand. When he had said this, such brightness shone upon the town in which he was born that all who had come to the funeral of so great a father, as if in a rapture of mind, saw his spirit raised up by an angel in a cloud, and penetrating the heavens with the brightness of the cloud, and the brightness flying with him no longer appeared at all. Thus, bathed in a stream of sacred blood, the true martyr and confessor departed in peace, on the day before the Kalends of July.

These things were done by the heretics on the seventh day before the Kalends of June, and in that same year blessed Eleutherius fell asleep in peace, in the reign of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom is honour and power through all ages of ages. Amen.
SERMON ON THE INCARNATION OF THE LORD.

Fatherly authority exhorts brotherly charity to believe, and gently entreats it to cease from evil. We cry out, and no mortal heeds. We call on Christ, and the heavenly Christ hears. Nevertheless, let the unbelieving listen faithfully, let the foolish understand wisely. We believe in God the Father almighty, creator of things visible and invisible. We adore Christ, the perfect Son of the perfect [Father]. We venerate the Paraclete, the Spirit proceeding from both. Just as the Father is without beginning, so also the Son, whose Father is God, remains without beginning. The Only-begotten, coming forth from the Unbegotten, was always God, who always remained the Son, whose Father we confess to be God. Before the world was made the Father had the Word, possessed wisdom, and did not lack power. The catholic Fathers declare the Word to be the strength of God, the wisdom of God, which we do not doubt has always existed. And that we may believe more surely that this wisdom existed from the beginning, let us hear what it plainly says: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High. For when the Most High established the firmament, made firm the earth, and the fountain of water broke forth from the deep abyss, I was in the highest places with the Father, ordering all things with him. And again it is said: All wisdom is from the Lord God, and has been with him always, and is before the ages. And that the Father himself might show that the Word existed from the beginning, he declares more plainly, saying: My heart has uttered a good Word (Ps. 44:1). We believe him to be God in such a way that the Father remains always: since his Word, Wisdom and Strength is the Son. Indeed the prophets proclaimed the childbearing of the Virgin Mary. For concerning the birth of Christ the prophet Isaiah testifies, saying: Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb and bear a son, and he shall be called Counsellor, mighty God; whose power and dominion shall endure for ever (Isa. 9:7). So Christ, the Only-begotten of the unbegotten Father, was born according to the flesh from the seed of David, made a visible man, whose Father is the invisible God. It was indeed necessary for the human race that him whom the Father had begotten invisible from the beginning a virgin should conceive, a virgin should bring forth visible to us, and remain a virgin after the birth; and that Christ should be in God (perhaps: from God), begotten before all ages without union with a woman from the heavenly Father, and should be born a perfect man from a virginal womb, without a fleshly father. For the Holy Spirit, entering the virgin hall of chastity, caused such a Christ, made man, to come forth from her, as would restore what was lost and remit the sins of all, who, innocent, would pour out his innocent blood for the redemption of human frailty, and through whom, a visible man, the invisible God would present his only-begotten as visible to men. So Jesus Christ was born according to the flesh and on the eighth day was circumcised. In the circumcision of his flesh, just as circumcision came to its end, so through the baptism of Christ the consecration of baptism had its beginning. For the water of the Jordan did not sanctify him by washing him, but the Son of God purified those waters by entering them. Therefore, as the Father had foretold through his prophets, a virgin conceived, and the creature brought forth her creator to the earth. [We] testify that he rose on the third day after his passion and ascended into the heavens while the apostles watched. Concerning his glorious passion the apostle Paul, writing to the Philippians, says: Who, though he was in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in appearance as a man: he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross (Phil. 2). We, then, holding this about God, do not call him who was born of the Virgin Mary a mere man, nor do we preach separately one son of man and another Son of God, lest we make one person of the flesh and another of the Godhead; but in the Word of God and in the flesh we profess and believe one Christ, and we bear witness to and worship him as the only-begotten Son by nature. This too we declare openly, that the Word of God likewise took a beginning of flesh and blood, and made our body specially his own, and came forth a perfect man from the virgin, yet without casting off the heavenly Godhead, so as to lose that generation which he had from the eternal Father. This the reasoning of the catholic faith certainly attests. In this religion, we have learned, were the holy Fathers and the chosen soldiers of God and true athletes, who truly believed the mother of our Lord Jesus Christ to be a virgin: not because the Godhead and nature of the Word took its beginning in her, but because that most sacred body of Christ, animated by a rational soul, was born from the undefiled womb of that same virgin; and we know that the Word of God, united to it substantially, was born in the flesh. Hence the apostle Paul, writing to the Thessalonians about him, says: For they themselves report concerning you what kind of entrance we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised up, Jesus, who has delivered us from the wrath to come. We, then, worshippers of this holy faith and followers of the Christian law, profess that the Word of God was united to flesh according to substance, and that one Christ, God and the same man, is to be adored together with his own flesh. We testify with a true heart, we declare with a pure mind, we confess with a modest mouth, that the Son of God was crucified in the flesh, endured death in the flesh, and was made the firstborn from the dead, inasmuch as in him the perfect life of believers abides, who as God is the giver of life to all the faithful.

These things, most beloved, I write so that the peace and concord of the Churches may be preserved, and the indissoluble bond of charity may remain, and the gifts of divine bounty may not be diminished. We venerate the Trinity in unity and believe that the Father and the Son were so in the beginning, as we confess and worship the Paraclete proceeding from both: not three gods, but only one God, to whom let us faithfully pay what is owed, so that our Lord and Redeemer may not disdain to forgive us our offences, who, wonderful, works such great miracles in his servants; and we shall see greater things than these, with the help of him whose majesty and beauty, unfading glory, power and inestimable honour endure for ages of ages. Amen.
SERMON ON THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD.

Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation. Behold, in these days we see fulfilled what is said by the voice of the prophet Isaiah: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel. Behold, a virgin conceived without man's seed; a virgin gave birth without any violation of the flesh. For by the birth of this son the joy of the human people is increased; by his rising the enemy of our substance is confounded with grief. For that adversary of ours, who rose at dawn like Lucifer, who delighted in the foods of the delights of God's paradise, fell from heaven and deserved to hear: If you are exalted like an eagle, from there you will be shamefully dragged down by the Lord. That enemy of the human substance, who had said he was like the Most High, having fallen through pride, roaring like a lion, seeks whom he may devour. He does not seek the unbelieving man, nor the wrathful, nor those who are outside, but seeks the humble, the modest, the reasonable, or strives to cast down someone of the Church of Christ. This envious one sent man, cast out of God's paradise, into this misery and valley of tears, and wished to put blessed Job far from God, but could not. For of that spotless and simple man it is said: His strength is in his loins, and his power in his navel. So through the disobedience of the first man death and misery entered the world; but through the birth of the second man salvation and joy came in. A star gave forth the sun: a Virgin [gave forth] God-man without a man; a rod brought forth a flower. If Mary had not remained a virgin, she would certainly not have borne the Son of God. O how praiseworthy is virginity! Most blessed Isaiah says: A rod has come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from his root (Isa. 11:1). The virgin is the mother of Christ, simple, humble and spotless, with no seed attaching from outside, and fruitful by a union after the image of God. It was truly necessary for men that a virgin should conceive the Son of God, grievous indeed to Satan, but fruitful for us. Of that flower which the rod of Jesse brought forth it is written: I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys. If virginity did not profit a virgin, the prophet would not have signified that a Virgin was to be born of a Virgin. Good indeed is the continence of widows, but better is virginal chastity. But the law of Moses had been given otherwise. For it is written: Blessed is he who has seed in Zion. And: Cursed is the barren woman who does not bear. And elsewhere: There was no feeble one among their tribes. But in the law of our Lord Jesus Christ it is said: Rejoice, barren one, and do not think yourself a dry tree. You shall have a place in place of sons and daughters for ever. Now also he who is weak is made stronger, as the Apostle testifies, who says: I will gladly glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may dwell in me. Therefore, because Christ was begotten before all ages from the eternal Father, this was the ineffable mystery of divine power; but that he appeared to us visible as a man from a virgin, this was the grace of human salvation. Death entered the world through Eve; but lost life is restored through Mary. After the Virgin conceived him in her womb, the Virgin brought forth the light that enlightens every man coming into this world: whose government is upon his shoulder, who is the mighty God, father of the age to come (Isa. 9). The curse pronounced against the whole human race was loosed. But who could fathom this secret of the divine counsel, that a Virgin should receive in her womb, a Virgin should bring forth God begotten of the Father before all things without a mother, and the invisible God should appear through a visible man, and, taking on death by the condition of human mortality, conceived by no law of bodily generation, should come forth from a womb of human origin under the human law, and his Mother herself should remain an uncorrupted virgin? So Christ, born before the ages without a mother from an invisible father, not out of need for himself but for the human race, is born a second time without a fleshly father from a visible mother. And because we were imperilled through the disobedience of the first woman, it was fitting that we be saved through a woman. Let the human race rejoice, for Christ is born, and, wrapped in cheap cloths, is laid in the manger of animals. The cheapness of the cloths is indeed a great and unspeakable mystery. For that cheapness of cloths is adored by the Magi, and to the child himself, lying in the manger and reigning over the angelic creation, gold, frankincense and myrrh are offered. Gold befits a king, the offering of frankincense a great priest, and myrrh the burial of the dead. Gold signifies that the Son of God, born of the Virgin, already reigns on earth; frankincense that the high priest offers himself for us as a victim to the heavenly Father; myrrh that the same Son of the Virgin is buried and rises again for the salvation of the human race. The cloths, then, with which the Virgin mother binds the infant, we know to be our sins, as the prophet says: Truly he bore our infirmities, and he himself carried our sins. Through these cheap cloths it is plain that he took on our offences. That he is placed between two animals is an inestimable mystery of God. Behold, fulfilled is what is said by the voice of the prophet Habakkuk: Lord, I heard your report and was afraid; I considered your works and trembled: in the midst of two animals. And fittingly the Son of man is placed among lowly animals. For he is the life of men, the food of angels, and the fodder of beasts. It was fitting, therefore, that he who was the living bread should be placed crying in a cradle between two animals. For he it is who says: I am the living bread, who came down from heaven. He is the clean Lamb, whose unblemished body, after it has been handled by the priest and eaten by all the faithful people, remains unharmed and unconsumed. So after what the prophets had foretold and the patriarchs proclaimed about the Virgin's childbearing was fulfilled, and all things completed that were to be done concerning Christ through the angel Gabriel, it was fitting that the new man, coming forth clean from man, a virgin come forth from a virgin, should gain for himself a new household: that he who was adored by angels in heaven should also appoint angels for himself on earth. Then he willed to be baptized by John, the king by a soldier, the Lord by a servant; not because he had committed any crimes, but that our sins might be blotted out through his baptism. For the water did not cleanse him, but he who baptized in Spirit and truth blessed it by his entering. Then, announcing to the people the word of life and truth, he makes some disciples, and others evangelists. For the twin brothers, that is James and John, leaving their father Zebedee and the boat, followed the Saviour, with one mind setting aside the care of the household and the affection of blood. After these came many other disciples, to whom the Lord Jesus said: If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For so divine Scripture holds. No soldier goes to battle with his wife. If anyone wishes to follow the footsteps of the Redeemer, let him leave all things, and not look back behind him, as Lot's wife looked: for no one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God. But if anyone has the means to redeem his soul from the enemy's deceit, let him feed the poor, practise hospitality, cover the naked even with a cheap garment. When Christ wished to ascend from earth to heaven, and pass from hell to the higher places, as he had long before foretold to his disciples, he endured death to free the dead from sin. He preached to show us the way of salvation. He rose again to make those brought to life live. Following his footsteps, dearest ones, let us not please ourselves, but God and our neighbour. For so Jesus, when he announced peace to the people, said to the disciples: I have not come to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. For when the Son of man fulfilled the will of God, the Jews said that he sinned against God; they rather, by not receiving the Son whom he had sent, reproached the Father, and so they fastened the Son of God, who had committed nothing, to the gibbet of the cross without cause. The sins of sinners therefore fell upon Christ, who, found innocent, was killed as a blasphemer. Then the Lord Jesus, victorious, despoiling the places of darkness, rose on the third day and happily ascended into the heavens from which he had descended. And how did the humanity ascend, unless the Godhead first descended into the lower parts of the earth, to be united to human nature? For the heavenly Godhead descended so that the Redeemer's humanity might ascend. He is one and the same person. For he was always in the Father, always with the Father, always together with the Father. After the ascension of the humanity he sent the Holy Spirit, appearing to the disciples in tongues of fire. The Spirit is indeed the power of the Son, which went out from him and healed all. Yet he is said to proceed from the Father, and is usually referred to him, from whom both he is and that which is his. For Christ himself declares, saying: My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me. For the Son has it from the Father that he is God; for he is God from God. From him he has it that the Holy Spirit proceeds from him. Therefore, dearest brothers, let us celebrate with due veneration the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Let us flee pride, lest we be overwhelmed in hell like the evil angels. For through pride a man is puffed up, through avarice he is shaken, in ambition he delights. Do not glory in worldly riches; do not seek to be preferred to others, lest an evil thought creep in; and you who now covet gilded garments, let it rather please you to sit in squalor, so that you too may please Christ, to whom is honour with the invisible Father through all ages of ages. Amen.
SERMON FOR THE FEAST OF THE ANNUNCIATION.

Dearest brothers, a few things must be said about the threefold solemnity of the most blessed Virgin Mary, in which the angel announces, the Virgin conceives, and the Only-begotten Son of the Unbegotten is clothed in flesh. Yet manifold praise is due to him who announces, more to her who conceives through the ear, and most of all to him who is conceived. This is the saving day, to be celebrated by us with due veneration, which reconciles earthly things to heavenly. On it the divinity of the Redeemer descended to us, so that our humanity might ascend to the heavens. This is that solemn day which takes its beginning from the angel: how he announced that the virgin [Son] would be born of a Virgin, how the power of the Most High overshadowed the Virgin, how the God who cannot be touched deigned to be touched, he who is the eternal light that enlightens every man coming into this world. This is the solemn day which lifts and raises us from earth to the heights, and exalts us with honour above the heavens of heavens, as the present sermon will make plain to you. For when the first man had been cast out because of the tree of knowledge, forbidden by the Lord and wrongly tasted, the deceit of demons deceived men as they wandered through the enticements of vice; by deceiving, it took them captive, and by taking them captive, it plunged them into the outer darkness. There weeping and gnashing of teeth is heard, as the Lord testifies. For when the devil's glory had stirred up ambition, and ambition had provoked envy, he grieved that the human race was to be carried from earth to heaven. Since he himself had fallen wretchedly, he found by this a consolation for his own misery. The Father, therefore, considering the perdition of the human race through the serpent's deceit, deigned to free the world through the incarnation of his Only-begotten Son, so that, since woman had been cast out of the seats of paradise through the urging of demons, she might through the greeting of an angel merit to receive the glory of immortality. The urging of the enemy deceived Eve; the greeting of Gabriel strengthened Mary. The angel announces, so that the devil's deceit may be destroyed; the Virgin is overshadowed by the power of the Most High at the angel's announcement, so that woman, long since deceived by Satan's messenger, may be restored. The incorruptible God is clothed in flesh and descends, so that through this second man, Jesus, the old man might ascend, who, having wrongly tasted the fruit, came down to this misery and vale of tears. For we read that when the woman had deceived her husband, the Lord said to her: In pain you shall bear children, and your turning shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you. These three hardships are suffered by all women who do not imitate Mary's virginity; as if the Lord said to her: When your turning is to your husband, you will be subject to his service; and when you give birth, you will suffer the harms of pain and sorrow. But these three are shut out from the happiness of the Virgin Mary, and not only from the Virgin herself, but from all women who have vowed their virginity to Christ. Come then, virgins, who vow your virginity to the Virgin: vow your bodily integrity to the Virgin who showed the Lord an unblemished chastity. Hear, then, of how great merit this Virgin was. For she merited not only to be visited by an angel's address, but to contain within the enclosure of her virginal womb him who could in no way be contained. Our mother Eve is weighed down by three evils, but blessed Mary is shut out from them and rejoices in a threefold happiness. For she is strengthened by the angel's greeting, once strengthened she is blessed, and she is told that she will be fruitful in the fullness of grace. For thus it is written: The angel was sent to a virgin. We confess this to be the virgin of whom we read in Isaiah: A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse (that is, the Virgin Mary), and a flower shall rise up from its root, that is, Christ. For he himself declares in the Song of Songs, saying: I am the flower of the field. And coming in to her he said: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. O angelic voice, full of sweetness and joy! When he said, Hail, Mary, he offered the Virgin a heavenly greeting. When he said, Full of grace, he showed that the sentence was annulled by which our first parents were made far from God, and that the grace of heavenly blessing was restored, by which, freed from servitude, they were led into paradise. And when he uttered, Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb, he declared blessed not only the fruit of her womb, but [the fruit] of all women who, following the Virgin Mary, remain in virginity. O blessed Virgin, O Virgin chosen out by the Maker of the world! You will conceive him who was begotten before all ages, without a mother, from the eternal Father, made a mother without union with any man. For there the ear was the wife, and the angel's word was the husband. A virgin you will conceive, and after giving birth you will remain a virgin, and the Son of God will descend into you, so that he who was to ascend in the power of his loftiness and the glory of his brightness to the East may turn the grace of his majesty to the West. Do not let what you hear confound you, nor the conception trouble you. For this conception is not a necessity, but the inestimable power of God. He will be clothed in flesh and will hide himself in your virginal womb, and the Son of God will begin to be the son of man, remaining always what he was. For we believe him unchangeable, yet mercifully taking up what he was not, so that he whom the whole world could not carry might be contained in you. Through this conception virginal chastity will not be lessened; rather, the integrity of chastity will be increased in you. You became the Mother of the Maker while he was with the Father; and when he was born of you, his Mother, he remained with the Father. For he is always with the Father, since, being without beginning, he has no beginning in time. For he is always with the Father, who remains without beginning and end. You have become a heavenly ladder; as the rod of Aaron you have flowered above the rest, that is, you have shone above the rest, worthy in virginity. You have become a ladder by which heavenly glory descended to the lower world, so that lowliness might be carried up to the heights of heaven. O new and unheard-of joining! O ineffable and wondrous mingling! He who had created all things from nothing is created; he who could not be contained is contained; he who makes all overflow with riches is made poor; Christ, who is perfect, deigns to empty himself. For he is said to have emptied himself of the form of the Godhead in time, so that we might be enriched by his heavenly perfection. Therefore, dearest brothers, let us entreat the Virgin to reconcile God to men and bring earthly things into concord with heavenly. May she intercede for what is past, beseeching her Son for what is to come. O Virgin, give not only bodily food, but the bread of angels that descended within the enclosure of your womb; make us fear the Son of God. For the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. For if anyone fears the Lord, he will keep his commandments; then purification of the flesh will follow, so that we may be able to behold the rays of the divine light. For after purification of the flesh is given us, the enlightenment of our heart will follow. Hear, then, and incline your ear to our prayers. O Virgin, who are rightly praised by us, who, remaining a virgin after giving birth, are venerated by us, pray God for us, that he may grant constancy and bestow patience; that concord may be made firm and forbearance increased; so that, when the pain of grief and misery, of calamity and sorrow, comes, you may deign to present us to your Only-begotten Son, who is one God, whom we confess one in substance, three in persons; who is through all, and above all, and in us all; who is in part searched out and in part known; who does not will the death of the sinner, but that he be turned from his evil way. Pray that we may be made perfect light, that we may praise you together in the glory of your Son, to whom is honour and power through all ages of ages. Amen.
PRAYER OF BLESSED ELEUTHERIUS, AS HE WAS DYING, TO GOD FOR THE FAITH AND THE CHURCH
OF TOURNAI.

The Catholic faith believes and confesses, adores and venerates, not three gods but one God. Unity remains in Trinity; perfect Trinity consists in unity. True God, the same our Lord Jesus Christ, was born of the true Father according to divinity; but according to humanity he was begotten of an unblemished virgin. From both proceeds the Holy Spirit, who may cause the hearts of unbelievers to be converted to the knowledge of the truth. The Son is equal to the Unbegotten Father, the Holy Spirit equal to his Only-begotten Son. The Son proceeded as eternal light from eternal light; an unfailing lamp shone out from that invisible brightness when the Virgin Mary, foretold as Mother of the eternal Judge, conceived of the Holy Spirit, and, remaining a virgin in chastity, brought forth the Son of God to the earth, and after the wondrous birth, continuing in virginity, nourished Christ Jesus with divine milk. O that holy angelic announcement! The angel Gabriel is sent to the Virgin, who knew nothing of the mystery. The Mother of the Redeemer likens herself to a handmaid when she answers the angel; for she says: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to your word. So the Son of God, made flesh, so that the angel's word might be fulfilled, is born of the glorious Virgin by divine inspiration; he is laid in a manger, then announced to shepherds by an angel. Reigning in heaven, he rules all things, and the Son of God lies as a little child in a manger. He is nursed by a virgin mother, and adored by the Magi with gifts. To show us the humility of his power and the magnificence of his divinity, he deigned to possess all things as a man, without sin. He had no sin, he endured death, and by his death he gave us immortal life. O wondrous birth of the Only-begotten of God! O marvellous preaching of the son of man! O unheard-of wisdom of so young a man! The Son of God had come forth in the synagogues, and through the Holy Spirit he refutes all the scribes and doctors of the law; yet not as though that same Spirit conferred any power on him in so far as he is the Son of God. For the Son, who is coeternal with the eternal Father, never needed another's help, for he is perfect and blessed for ages of ages. The wise marvel at a wisdom unheard of in the world. For this reason the Jews scourge the son of man, betrayed by Judas, the impious and most wicked traitor, and pursue him with insults. And so Christ Jesus, who for the salvation of human frailty bowed himself to a voluntary self-emptying, offered his own body, not for himself but for our redemption, to the eternal Father as a true victim, a victim pleasing to God for an odour of sweetness. For what sacrifice or offering would he need, since as God he was free from all sin? For if all have sinned and need the grace of God, it is because human nature fell sick through sins and evil deeds; but he was not so, although he took the likeness of a servant and underwent death by his own free will. The prophet David had in mind the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ when he said: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a sovereign spirit (Psalm 50). For the Father is the beginning of all things, with whom the Son made all things: King of kings, father of the universe, and restorer of a failing world. Amid these words the pain of his wounds and of his soul pressed hard upon the holy man. What was he to do? He saw the day of his death drawing near, and knew that the churches he had built within the walls would fall. So, turning with tears, he prayed, saying:

Almighty and most merciful God, who willed that your glorious name be invoked with a threefold invocation in your three holy patriarchs, namely Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, so that through your only-begotten Son Jesus the excellent worshippers of the catholic faith might recognise, and perfectly believe, that in the perfect Trinity you are God the Father, Unbegotten, equal to the Only-begotten Son, and alike to the Holy Spirit: true Father, who begot the true Son before the foundation of the world and before the settling of things, who sent from heaven the Holy Spirit proceeding from you to strengthen the hearts of your disciples and to make the name of Christ glorious among men; whose true Trinity consists in unity, and one Godhead abides in Trinity, equal to the Son, equal to the Holy Spirit. For nothing is greater than you, nothing less than another. For you are the same God everywhere; everywhere is your majesty, your dominion, your power; you formed all things from nothing through your Only-begotten; you, descending into the womb of the undefiled Virgin, deigned to take the form of our servitude, and as perfect God to put on perfect man, so that, made flesh, he might come to the help of men, and, become man incarnate, might turn unbelievers to the way of truth. After the Virgin's childbirth, laid as a child in the cradle, he showed in himself the lowliness of [our] condition; he was shown by rejoicing angels to the shepherds keeping watch, and to the Magi of Ethiopia with a star going before them; he endured the temptations of the devil and, for us, reproaches and other torments, to free us from the snares of visible and invisible enemies and wipe away the stains of our crimes; he bore the gibbet of the cross to restore us to the glory of the heavenly court, which we lost through Adam; and the Son of man became incarnate to make the sons of men sons of God and sharers in heavenly goods. I entreat you, who became the author of our resurrection, so that you might open to us the entrance to heaven and take captive the dominion of the devil, and, ascending into heaven by your wonderful power, lead our captivity captive; who by your death gave life to the dead, and healing to the captives. I call upon you in your clemency, I appeal to you in your mercy, that you keep and defend, raise up and exalt the churches of Tournai, which I have raised up as far as my littleness could, and all the dwellings of the saints, from every disturbance of demons. Guard my few sheep, those present and those to follow, to the last generation, so that they may know that you are gentle, Father of mercy and goodness, giver of knowledge and truth. And to those who have pursued me, your unworthy servant, with swords and clubs even to death, grant kindly pardon, and deign to gather me with your saints into your granary. And to those also, most loving God, who devoutly honour my memory, grant faith, bestow friendship, most merciful God, according as your clemency is not unaware [how they] delight in the catholic faith and in the Christian religion. For all things are naked and open to your eyes. Behold, now the time of my dissolution draws near. Eternal God, what shall I do? Let me follow David, who says: As the hart longs for the springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God. And again he says: My soul has thirsted for the living God; when shall I come and appear before the face of God? If it can be, allow me to be likened to blessed Job, who says: I am compared to mud and likened to embers and ashes. In you I trust, my God; you I seek, you I long to see, whom I always worshipped while placed on earth, to whom I have devoted myself with all my love: free me, you who are blessed for ever and ever.

And soon, breaking out again into the praises of God, he said: The catholic faith declares him to be the Son to whom the Father cries through the prophet, saying: You are my Son, today I have begotten you. And again: With you is the beginning in the day of your power, in the splendours of the saints; from the womb before the morning star I begot you. He is Jesus Christ our Lord, equal to the Father, invisible, proceeding from the invisible, eternal from the eternal, immortal from the immortal; who, uniting to himself the nature of our humanity according to subsistence, underwent birth from that bodily and virginal womb. Not that he needed that glorious birth of necessity, but in order to sanctify the very first-fruits of our substance; so that, when Christ united with flesh had come forth from the blessed Virgin Mary, that so wretched curse which had been pronounced against the whole human race might cease, and no longer destine souls and mortal bodies to death; and to show to be true what he had foretold by the voice of the prophet: Death is swallowed up in victory. And elsewhere: God has taken away every tear from every face. He is Christ, the son of the Virgin Mary, who restored hearing to the deaf and sight to the blind; he walked on the sea with dry feet, put demons to flight, calmed winds and seas, cleansed lepers, healed paralytics, raised the dead, and said to the unbelieving Jews: If you do not believe my words, at least you ought to believe the mighty works and miracles. There is one Son of God in Christ, who, just as he is in truth the invisible Son of God, so is in truth the visible Christ. For perfect God put on perfect man, to bestow perfect salvation on men. And concerning the Holy Spirit let us hear the prophet praying and saying: Do not take your Holy Spirit from me. It is indeed great rashness to separate the Son from the Father, the Father from the Son, [or to treat] the Holy Spirit as if not proceeding from both. For God is inseparable, unchangeable and impassible. The Son, as was said above, is equal to the Father; the Holy Spirit is neither higher nor better than he, but alike to the Father, equal to the Son, proceeding from both. Almighty God sent the Holy Spirit into the world, the Unbegotten, so that he might glorify the Only-begotten, his Son. But because Christ the Son of God performed miracles for men, healed lepers, raised the dead, and did other things unheard of in the world, and to demonstrate his Godhead made use of the power of his own Spirit, he was said to be glorified by him. Yet it is not fitting to affirm that our Lord Jesus Christ was glorified by the Holy Spirit as one who through him used a power not his own, and took up through that same Spirit power against unclean spirits; rather we ought to confess that it was his own Spirit through which he did such splendid miracles. It is fitting also for every believer to affirm that he offered an offering or sacrifice to the Father not for himself but for the redemption of the human race, since he needed no offering, who, undefiled, knew no sin. Therefore let the catholic faith believe and affirm that the flesh made [his] is life-giving and the very own flesh of the Word himself. For being Life by nature, as God, because he was united to his own flesh, he declared it life-giving. And when he says: Amen, amen I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, you will not have eternal life, we must not, however, think of it as [the flesh] of a mere man. For according to its own nature, how could the flesh of a mere man be life-giving? Let the unhappy Jew flee; let the heretic who denies the birth of Christ be destroyed. The faithful praise together God, three in persons but one God in subsistence: whom the wretched, given over to the pains of hell, await in wrath, in whose company the evil angels rejoice; but the just await him for the reward of their labours, in whose fellowship the angels of God rejoice; with the help of him whose benefits are granted to the weak, through whom joy is given to the afflicted: to whom be honour, dominion and power, with the Unbegotten Father and the Holy Spirit, through endless ages of ages. Amen.
